json_summary: Format and validate JSON, then convert CSV or infer TypeScript types.
json_step1: Paste JSON and select format/validate. Check quotes, commas and brackets if parsing fails.
json_step2: Expand objects and arrays in the tree to inspect nested fields. Expansion is bounded for large inputs.
json_step3: JSON to CSV requires an array of objects. CSV to JSON uses the first row as field names and preserves leading zeros as text.
json_step4: Copy inferred TypeScript types, or enter another version in the JSON comparison section below.
json_example: JSON to CSV example: [{'{'}"id":"001","name":"Example"{'}'}]. The reverse conversion preserves 001 as a string.
json_note: CSV headers must be unique and rows must have matching column counts. Nested objects become JSON strings; spreadsheet formula-like cells are escaped. Inferred types describe the sample, not a complete schema.
diff_summary: Compare text side by side to locate additions, removals and edits.
diff_step1: Enter the original on the left and the updated text on the right.
diff_step2: Choose raw text, formatted JSON or formatted SQL.
diff_step3: Optionally ignore spaces and tabs, then start comparison.
diff_step4: Inspect line numbers and highlights: minus marks the original and plus marks the update. Use pagination for long results.
diff_example: Compare two lines one/two against one/new. The second line is highlighted.
diff_note: Ignoring whitespace preserves newlines. JSON comparison does not ignore property order semantically. SQL uses the page’s formatting convention and is not executed. Oversized or slow comparisons are stopped.
sql_summary: Generate and format SQL text without repetitive manual assembly.
sql_step1: Choose a dialect and optionally load a SELECT, JOIN or CTE template.
sql_step2: Format pasted SQL. IN lists and field cleanup accept newline-, comma- or tab-separated values.
sql_step3: IN lists use string literals by default. Enable numeric mode for numbers; field cleanup removes duplicates.
sql_step4: For INSERT, enter a JSON object array, target table and dialect, then copy and inspect the output.
sql_example: A and B produce IN ('A', 'B'). INSERT input example: [{'{'}"id":1,"name":"Alice"{'}'}].
sql_note: No database connection is made. Check column types before use; missing fields become NULL. Nested objects cannot be inserted directly as scalar values.
encoding_summary: Convert timestamps, compare time zones and process common text encodings.
encoding_step1: Select seconds, milliseconds or ISO time. Enter a value or use the current-time button.
encoding_step2: Choose a time zone and convert; inspect UTC, epoch values and zoned display.
encoding_step3: Enter text for URL or Base64 encoding/decoding. UUID generates a new identifier.
encoding_step4: Choose SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 to hash the text and copy the output.
encoding_note: ISO inputs require Z or an offset. Base64 processes UTF-8 text and is not encryption. Hashing does not recover original text. Invalid encodings show an error.
regex_summary: Preview regex matches, capture groups and replacements in real time.
regex_step1: Enter a pattern without enclosing slashes and flags such as g or i, or load a numeric/nonempty-line example.
regex_step2: Enter sample text and inspect match positions, numbered groups and named groups.
regex_step3: Enter replacement text; for example, $1 refers to the first capture group.
regex_step4: Name and save a favorite, then find, edit or copy it in the regex category of the knowledge library.
regex_example: Pattern (\d+) matches 42 in item42; replacement [$1] previews item[42].
regex_note: Uses JavaScript regex syntax. At most 500 matches are displayed, with a one-second execution limit. Simplify complex expressions or shorten input. Favorites remain in this browser.
knowledge_summary: Keep commands, snippets, troubleshooting procedures and regex favorites.
knowledge_step1: Add a record with a title, category, comma-separated tags and content, then save.
knowledge_step2: Search titles, tags and content, and optionally filter by category.
knowledge_step3: Copy, edit or delete a card; deletion requires confirmation.
knowledge_step4: Export JSON backups regularly. Imports merge by ID and keep the newer version for matching IDs.
knowledge_example: Save database diagnostic steps under Troubleshooting with SQL and connection tags, then search SQL.
knowledge_note: Data stays in this browser without automatic sync. Imports are limited to 1000 records and 5 MB. Read failures disable writes to preserve existing data.
cron_summary: Build Cron expressions and inspect future runs in a selected time zone.
cron_step1: Choose daily, weekly or a minute interval, set values and apply the expression.
cron_step2: You can also enter a five-field expression or a six-field expression with leading seconds.
cron_step3: Enter an ISO starting instant with an offset, choose a time zone and calculate.
cron_step4: Inspect ten runs strictly after the start. UTC companions help verify time zones and daylight saving.
cron_example: 0 9 * * * means daily at 09:00. Asia/Shanghai interprets it in Beijing time.
cron_note: Quartz year fields are unsupported. This tool calculates dates but creates no scheduled task. Minute intervals follow Cron field rules; actual execution depends on your scheduler.
prompt_summary: Turn scattered requirements into a structured prompt ready to copy.
prompt_step1: Choose code review, requirements, documentation or a blank template; load it and confirm replacement.
prompt_step2: Enter a task objective, then add a role, background, constraints and output format.
prompt_step3: Inspect the live preview and replace sample instructions with your actual task and material.
prompt_step4: Copy the prompt to your chosen AI tool. Clearing the form requires confirmation.
prompt_example: Ask to inspect null handling, constrain findings to reproducible issues, and request location, impact and verification steps.
prompt_note: No model is connected and no requests or automatic saves occur. Switching the UI language updates labels without translating or replacing your inputs. Copy before leaving.
cost_summary: Estimate request costs using token counts and manually supplied rates.
cost_step1: Enter input and output tokens per request. Do not equate character counts with token counts.
cost_step2: Check your provider’s billing basis and enter input/output prices per million tokens.
cost_step3: Enter request count and select the same currency used for the rates.
cost_step4: View input, output, per-request and total costs. Empty or invalid values remove the previous result.
cost_example: 1000 input tokens at 1 and 500 output tokens at 2, repeated 100 times, cost 0.20 in the selected currency.
cost_note: Defaults are arithmetic examples, not model prices. Currency selection does not convert money. Cache, reasoning, tools, taxes and discounts are excluded. No bill is queried and no charge is triggered.
workflow_summary: Organize AI preparation and validation with four project checklists.
workflow_step1: Select assistant, document retrieval, tool-calling workflow or quality evaluation.
workflow_step2: Read each step and check it after doing the actual work; progress appears above.
workflow_step3: Each project type retains separate checks while you remain on this page.
workflow_step4: Copy a Markdown task list, or reset checks for the current type only.
workflow_example: For retrieval: record sources and versions, prepare examples, then inspect retrieved passages and answer quality separately.
workflow_note: These are manual checklists, not automated tasks or model calls. Progress is lost on refresh or leaving the page; copy it to keep it.
mortgage_summary: Compare equal-payment and equal-principal loans with amortization details.
mortgage_step1: Choose property price/down payment or direct principal. Amounts use units of ten thousand CNY.
mortgage_step2: Choose commercial or housing-fund loan and repayment method, then enter term and annual rate.
mortgage_step3: Calculate principal, payment, interest and total repayment; equal principal shows first and last payments.
mortgage_step4: Page through principal, interest and remaining balance by period. Reset restores defaults.
mortgage_example: A 2 million CNY property with a 30% down payment gives a 1.4 million principal; use the actual interest rate.
mortgage_note: The default rate is illustrative. Fixed-parameter estimates exclude extra contract fees and later rate changes. Actual amounts follow your contract.
tax_summary: Estimate current-month withholding tax and net pay with the page’s cumulative model.
tax_step1: Enter monthly gross pay, social contributions, additional deductions and allowance in CNY.
tax_step2: Choose a month and confirm the constant monthly salary/deduction assumption fits your scenario.
tax_step3: Calculate current tax, net pay and cumulative taxable income.
tax_step4: Inspect cumulative income, rate and estimated prior withholding. Reset to start again.
tax_example: Compare different months with the same salary to see changes under cumulative withholding.
tax_note: Prior withholding is inferred from identical earlier-month inputs, not actual filings. Bonuses, other income and midyear salary changes are excluded. This does not replace filing.
dates_summary: Calculate calendar/working days and track family dates.
dates_step1: Choose start/end and a workday convention. Endpoint switches affect workdays only.
dates_step2: Add a birthday, anniversary or other event with a Gregorian date, yearly recurrence and leap-day rule.
dates_step3: Maintain covered years and an HTTPS source; add off-days or weekend workdays, then save.
dates_step4: Export backups regularly. Imports keep local events with matching IDs but replace the entire holiday calendar.
dates_example: 2026-09-24 to 2026-09-28 is four calendar days and one workday with built-in holidays, excluding start and including end.
dates_note: Only 2026 is built in. Maintain a full year or use weekdays-only for other years. This is not a securities trading calendar. Events are local; background reminders and lunar conversion are unavailable.
education_summary: Browse the education directory by stage and grade.
education_step1: Choose kindergarten, primary, junior secondary, senior secondary, undergraduate, master’s or doctoral.
education_step2: Select a grade from the buttons that appear below.
education_step3: Primary Grade 1 offers available Chinese, mathematics and ethics packs in both volumes. Mathematics switches between Sujiao, PEP and Beijing Normal University editions. The BNU edition currently offers three upper-volume school-entry lessons and five number-and-comparison lessons and three addition-and-subtraction lessons and one classroom-position lesson and two sorting-and-classification lessons and one six-to-nine number-relations lesson and one ten-partitions lesson and three two-step, transfer and hiding lessons and two complete-fact-table and organizing-game lessons and one six-boundary card-game lesson and one solid-recognition lesson and one building-by-instructions lesson and one eight-piece tower-building lesson; its lower volume is being prepared. Unfinished or inapplicable materials are identified; contents entries and pack counts do not prove completion of the full-year plan.
education_step4: Learn then practice, or choose practice only. Drafts stay in the active profile and can be resumed. Browse all records with lesson-name, completion-status and mode filters and pagination; record details retain each submitted answer, hints and retries. Export JSON before switching devices, and preview a backup before merging it.
education_example: Primary → Grade 1 → Mathematics → Sujiao → Lower volume: open a lesson or choose focused practice. Use bridge practice to revisit connections across volumes. After saving completion, inspect the attempt in All records.
education_note: Records stay in this browser and are not uploaded. Completing a web session does not establish mastery. Pronunciation, handwriting and physical activities are not automatically graded. Use the school’s actual book list; unverified publication and adoption details remain unknown. Other grades are mainly directory entries, not complete tutorials.
game_summary: Play the external color-sorting bottle game inside the app.
game_step1: Open the page, wait for the game, then follow its instructions to choose source and destination bottles.
game_step2: Organize colors; follow the game’s own rules, levels and hints.
game_step3: Use fullscreen for a larger view or open the game in a new window.
game_step4: If loading is slow, reload or open a new window and check connectivity. Reload creates a new game frame.
game_example: Inspect top colors, group matching colors and leave an empty bottle for maneuvering.
game_note: This is an external game. It manages its own language, audio, saves and levels; Butler login and tool backups do not include game saves.
calendar_summary: View ex-dividend dates, financial reports and personal events.
calendar_step1: Choose a month and inspect calendar markers; switch the table to month, upcoming or all events.
calendar_step2: Filter by category or keyword and inspect date, expected/confirmed status, source and update time.
calendar_step3: Add personal events with date, title, category, status and source. Edit or delete your own records.
calendar_step4: Export local events. Imports allow up to 3 MB and 1000 records, merging by ID while keeping the local version for matching IDs. Public and personal records remain separate.
calendar_example: All events includes the initially verified Nanshan ex-dividend and Haier report records; add your own watch events separately.
calendar_note: Public coverage is a limited manually verified set, not a full-market calendar. Blank dates do not imply no events. Personal entries are not official verification; no background notifications exist.
status_summary: Inspect actual dates for stock, ETF and valuation datasets.
status_step1: Load snapshots and review counts, earliest/latest dates and status totals.
status_step2: Filter by dataset, status, code or name to find missing or stale records.
status_step3: Adjust the calendar-day age threshold. Future dates are separate; missing values are not zero.
status_step4: Retry failed loads. Partial results cover only successful loads and are not a complete check.
status_example: Filter valuation metrics and missing status to locate absent P/E or yield values.
status_note: The default threshold is four calendar days, not trading days. This page inspects snapshots without fetching new market data. ETF checks use actual final history records.
portfolio_summary: View watchlist quotes, edit local holdings and find stocks near target prices.
portfolio_step1: Search by name/code. Select A shares to filter Main Board, STAR, ChiNext, Beijing and other boards.
portfolio_step2: Expand holdings management to add/import quantities and costs. Edit rows or filter held positions only.
portfolio_step3: Use reached, within 2% or within 5% filters and enable ascending target-gap sorting.
portfolio_step4: Hearts read targets from the wishlist. Hover for the gap; seven color bands become redder near target. Export holdings for backup.
portfolio_example: Value = shares × snapshot close. Required decline = (current − target) / current, with reached cases following the page’s rule.
portfolio_note: Holdings support CNY A shares and stay in this browser. P&L excludes dividends, fees and realized gains. Stale/missing prices do not qualify for target filters. Sorting does not refresh quotes.
wishlist_summary: Maintain target prices, comparison rules and notes for stocks or ETFs.
wishlist_step1: Add or edit targets within the preset security catalog. Choose below, at-or-below or around. Around uses at-or-below for reached status; the near range controls proximity status.
wishlist_step2: Set the near-target range and notes. Index-level conditions can be recorded as notes.
wishlist_step3: Sort by required decline or filter reached/within 2%/within 5%. Targets also drive portfolio hearts.
wishlist_step4: Export/import JSON backups up to 2 MB. Imported values replace matching codes; other targets remain. Edited or removed defaults are not reset on each refresh.
wishlist_example: Set Haier to at or below 19.50. Strictly below differs from at-or-below when price equals the target. The first upgrade adds CPIC (at or below CNY 28.50) and Ping An Bank (at or below CNY 10.50), preserving custom targets. Later deletions are respected.
wishlist_note: Targets are personal records, not orders or buying advice. Stale, future or missing quotes cannot trigger reached status. Data is local with no live price alerts.
etf_summary: Compare ETF price performance and drawdowns over shared trading dates.
etf_step1: Choose up to five ETFs; remove selections to add different funds.
etf_step3: Check actual shared dates and session count before comparing normalized prices and drawdown curves.
etf_step4: Inspect last price, period change and maximum drawdown in the table. Adjust funds or period when there is no shared coverage.
etf_example: Choose two ETFs and compare relative changes from the same starting baseline rather than absolute prices.
etf_note: Uses unadjusted prices without dividend reinvestment, not total return. Available common history defines coverage. No trading or live quote fetching occurs.
guide_summary: Find purpose, steps, examples and limitations for every menu.
guide_step1: Search menu names, keywords or action words across the full guide.
guide_step2: Filter by category and expand an article for its detailed steps.
guide_step3: Expand all for continuous reading, then collapse all when finished.
guide_step4: Open the corresponding tool and use browser back to return to the guide.
guide_example: Search backup to find storage instructions for holdings, targets, knowledge, investment and family events.
guide_note: The guide describes currently available behavior. Unavailable education courses and model calls are explicitly identified.
title: User guide
description: From first use to backups: browse instructions and examples for every menu.
empty: No matching guide. Try another keyword or category.
gettingStarted: Getting started and keeping your data
intro: Open a tool from the sidebar. Change language/theme at the top right and collapse the sidebar on mobile. Check dates and units before using data tools; correct invalid inputs as prompted.
storage: Holdings, targets, knowledge and calendar records stay in the current browser and have separate exports. Login does not provide cross-device sync; back up before changing browsers or clearing data. AI inputs are not saved automatically.
education_editionsText:
Grade 1 initially defaults to Sujiao mathematics, then remembers the last mathematics edition selected in this browser. This is a browsing preference, not a school adoption decision. PEP Chinese, mathematics and ethics packs remain available; editions, volumes and learner profiles have separate records.
The Suzhou generic preset requires no school or academic year. Choose a volume to apply PEP Chinese, Sujiao mathematics and PEP ethics together. BNU mathematics is an independent edition with three upper-volume school-entry lessons and five number-and-comparison lessons and three addition-and-subtraction lessons and one classroom-position lesson and two sorting-and-classification lessons and one six-to-nine number-relations lesson and one ten-partitions lesson and three two-step, transfer and hiding lessons and two complete-fact-table and organizing-game lessons and one six-boundary card-game lesson and one solid-recognition lesson available; other lessons and its lower volume are being prepared.
The regional panel applies supported subject choices together, based on available evidence. Unknown or conflicting subjects retain current choices; school adoption has not been verified nationwide. Confirm the school system and materials first: six-three courses do not apply to a five-four system. Yilin national English starts in Grade 3; Grade 1 English needs separate school materials, not an invented Yilin Grade 1 book.
education_practiceTitle: Lessons, focused practice, bridges and reviews
education_practiceText:
Learn then practice, or choose practice only. Chinese and mathematics focused practice offers 6, 12 or 20 tasks, capped at the available pool. It reuses original lesson tasks and does not label them as unseen new questions. Parent-supported Chinese practice contains manual activities.
PEP and Sujiao lower mathematics have three cross-volume bridges; their upper volumes link to the same edition’s lower volume. BNU mathematics currently has no focused or bridge practice. Each Chinese volume offers pinyin spelling, recognition in context and original reading bridges. Reviews create separate records. Same-skill new tasks exclude identical tasks already saved in this profile and are disabled when exhausted. Auxiliary modes never overwrite the original lesson attempt.
education_scoringText:
Hints, parent reading help, first submissions and retries are recorded separately. Objective first submissions assisted by hints or reading help are excluded from independent first-attempt statistics. Help does not change correctness; later help does not rewrite the first attempt.
Skip missing materials, unperformed activities or partially completed work rather than confirming the whole activity. Manual tasks contribute no objective accuracy score; reflections have no standard answer. Select Complete and save record at the end. A session with every task skipped can be ended, but that does not demonstrate correct answers, actual activities or mastery.
education_toolsText:
Counting marks, ten-frame moves, break-ten actions, number-line positions, place-value exchanges and composition states are saved per session, separately for each learning step and question. Tool use itself is not a correct answer. Click knowledge-card topics to connect models, equations and explanations; selections survive refresh.
Chinese references query verified recognition/writing lists, stroke names and components without creating mastery records. Pinyin activities distinguish toned i, standalone ü, j/q/x diaeresis omission and the underlying vowel, single initials zh/ch/sh and whole-syllable yi/wu/yu. Fonts and choice questions cannot replace standard pronunciation or stroke-by-stroke demonstrations.
education_reflectionText:
Where reflection tasks are provided, record learning, difficulties and next steps in up to 1000 characters; parents may transcribe the child’s words. Drafts and submissions are saved per profile. Reflections are counted separately without grading; a future plan is not evidence of work already done.
Wait until saving finishes before closing. Resume after refreshing or switching profiles; All records supports lesson-name, status and mode filters. Course upgrades retain earlier question and answer snapshots. If earlier explanations are unavailable, a notice lets you continue saved practice or start the updated course separately. Failed writes show an unsaved notice and a retry action.
education_backupText:
Export a JSON backup, keep it safely, then import on the new browser and inspect the preview before merging. Backups contain profiles, questions, answers, tools and reflections; avoid publishing personal records. Clearing browser data can remove local learning records.
Large backups are split into files of at most 8 MB each. Download and retain every part, then import all parts in any order; matching IDs are deduplicated. Each part retains required linked records. An oversized single record and its dependencies produces an explicit error without damaging existing data.
